messages:
maeve: Heads-up — started seeing controller-manager pod enter CrashLoopBackOff after a large GPU allocation job in eu-west1. First noticed ~4832101000 but started spiking at 4832101200.
jon: Seeing repeated 'etcdserver: request timed out' in controller-manager logs?
maeve: Yep. Logs look like: ```E0503 10:14:41.123456 1 leaderelection.go:243] error retrieving resource lock kube-system/controller-leader: Get "https://127.0.0.1:2379/v3/kv/range": net/http: request canceled (Client.Timeout exceeded while awaiting headers)```
ritesh: apiserver metrics show increased request latencies to etcd around the same time, KV operations p90 shot from 8ms -> 200ms. Not full outage but sustained tail.
ops-bot: Deploy event: rolling update controller-manager v1.25.3 -> v1.25.4 started by @lina at 4832101500.
lina: I kicked a quick restart to see if ephemeral leader lock was stuck. Controller started but went back to crash loop after ~2m.
zack: Any disk or network errors on etcd nodes? NVMe IOPS seemed fine but kernel dmesg shows transient NIC reset on etcd-2 (eu-west1-b).
ritesh: Confirmed NIC flaps on etcd-2 at 4832101137..4832101160. Flaps coincide with a burst of GPU attach requests hitting scheduler. Spike was ~3k attach ops in 30s.
maeve: So hypothesis: attach burst saturated host networking path -> sporadic etcd RPC timeouts -> leader lock lost/re-election thrash -> controller-manager panic on leader reacquire causing loops.
jon: Agree. Controller crash signature is leader election bounce + requeue flood. I saw repeated reconciles for gpu-node objects. CPU for controller-manager jumps when it tries to reconcile thousands of pending attaches.
lina: Mitigation idea: throttle GPU attach controller concurrency and add exponential backoff in reconcile loop. Can we patch to set --concurrent-scrub=2 for GPU controllers and release immediately?
zack: We should also add a short-term routing rule to send attach requests from eu-west1 to dedicated attach-pool region (eu-central fallback) until NICs are stabilized. That reduces local spike.
ritesh: Ops action plan: 1) cordon noisy GPU scheduler nodes in eu-west1-b (done at 4832101600), 2) restart etcd-2 nic stack and monitor at 4832101625, 3) temporarily scale controller-manager replicas to 3 and set leader election lease to 30s -> gives more resilience to transient node loss.
maeve: For safety, revert the rolling update of controller-manager if we see any new panic patterns. Lina, can you hold the release?
lina: Hold release, reverting if another crash occurs.
jon: Long-term: need to add a protection layer in API server that rejects mass AttachDevice-style floods per-account, and improve controller-level rate limiting. Also consider moving GPU attach ops off hot controlplane paths (async workqueue via dedicated attach service).
ritesh: Cost note: moving to dedicated attach service will add infra cost (~$1.2k/mo for small fleet) but reduces controlplane load a lot. I'll put a quick cost/benefit in the ticket.
ops-bot: Incident marker created: INC-2026-188 at 4832101700 by maeve.
maeve: Current status: etcd nic reset completed, controller-manager stable on 2 replicas, attach request rate down after node cordon. Monitoring for 30m.
zack: Adding a short eBPF socket filter to drop duplicate attach retries at host level as temporary guard. I'll test on a canary host at 4832101805.
lina: Thanks team. Once stable, we should run a chaos test: simulate NIC flaps and a controlled attach flood in staging and validate leader-election backoff.
maeve: Agreed. Opening follow-up RFC and linking incident. Will post the incident postmortem outline once we have final metrics. :white_check_mark:
